newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Crippled ship still adrift in Pacific.
newsitem.headline: Crippled ship still adrift in Pacific.

text.p: A small ship with 290 passengers crammed on its deck remained adrift without power in the central Pacific on Thursday, but a rescue tug should reach it within a day, the ship's charterer said.
The 1,000-tonne MV Maasmond appealed for help on Tuesday after an fire in its engine room shut down its engine.
The ship was found by a Royal New Zealand Airforce Orion rescue plane on Wednesday drifting about 500 miles east of the Kiribati island of Tarawa.

The ship's charterer, Kiribati businessman Waysang Kumkee, said a tug had been dispatched to tow it back to Tarawa, but it was hoped another vessel with spare parts also on its way to the Maasmond would be able to help restart its engine.

The 64.5-metre (210-foot) ship was chartered to carry mostly Kiribati students and workers and 400 tonnes of cargo to Christmas Island from Tarawa, one of a group of coral atolls about 3,000 miles north-east of Sydney.
Kumkee told Reuters from Tarawa that the passengers still hoped to be able to complete their journey and that Christmas Island was running short of the supplies being carried as cargo.
The passengers and crew had enough food and water to last the three more days, he said.
"The only problem is that they might get too bored just sitting there drifting," Kumkee said.
The MV Maasmond is registered in Kingstown in St Vincent and Grenadines, according to the Lloyds List.
